terms.comment: In Plautus and Terence a sexual word, “to lie with” (Lewis & Short); not for petting an animal.

terms.gloss: stroke down, pat (a head, a back)
evidence: Ter. Haut. 762: quīn tibi caput dēmulceam
Gell. 5.14.12: cruraque ejus et manūs … linguā lēniter dēmulcet
terms.comment: Chremes pats his slave’s head when he is pleased with him; Androclus’s lion licks the hands of the man it knows. Rare (Lewis & Short), but plain and affectionate.

phrases.latin: Canem lēniter dēmulcē; ecce, caudam movet.
phrases.english: Pat the dog gently; look, he’s wagging his tail.

phrases.latin: nōn possum patī quīn tibi caput dēmulceam; accēde hūc, Syre
phrases.english: I can’t help patting your head; come here, Syrus

sources: Lewis & Short: permulceo · Lewis & Short: subigito · Lewis & Short: demulceo
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 359.
